repos: the ADK itself: decks, configuration and the schemas it validates against
the .chiplet format, the published schemas and the reference readers. Not a submodule of anything, which is why it is pinned in integration-refs.json instead
the IntM4TM2 interposer PDK, whose decks are tested against the KLayout the image ships
the interconnect PDK, which owns the method registry the assembly flow reads
the KiCad plugin, which vendors the .chiplet reader and declares its own Python pins
the GDS to KiCad converter, which reads the black-box pad vocabulary and declares its own Python pins
the assembly editor. Read through the API and never checked out: the only thing any contract reads from it is its gate workflow, and a 349 MB clone buys nothing
the documentation build, whose requirements file is one of the places the ecosystem's KLayout version is declared
the KiCad fork. Read through the API and never checked out, for the same reason as the studio and 2.1 GB more of it
this repository: the lockfile, the image that declares every pin, and the only place where more than one repository exists at once

mirrors: the assembly-DRC boundary manifest is the PDK-agnostic contract between the exporters and the deck
artifacts.why: chiplet-spec publishes the schema and the ADK validates against it. The two trees are only ever correct together, and no per-repository gate can see the other one.

mirrors: the vendored Python .chiplet reader inside the KiCad plugin, read by hyp_to_gds and the clobber guard. It caught up with the pin when the plugin re-vendored at the reader the pin carries, so it is compared here byte for byte; the plugin's own suite still pins its sha256 and the commit that carries it
checked_elsewhere: the vendored Python .chiplet reader. adk's suite compares it through git with the blob at the commit vendor/README.md declares, and reads that declaration with this same pattern
artifacts.why: the reference .chiplet reader and the vendored copies of it. A mirror is compared with the pin byte for byte. A copy checked elsewhere is taken at a commit its own tree declares, and that tree's suite checks it against that commit, which may be behind the pin; a byte comparison with the pin would be red on a lag that is declared and guarded, so this gate asserts the copy, the guard and the declaration are there and prints both versions. A copy that catches up with the pin returns to mirrors in the same commit. More copies are not listed here: staging.pin's inventory of the image's six chiplet_format_io copies (above STAGE_CHIPLET_SPEC_REF) names each one and what checks it, ci/check_vendored_reader.py among them.

mirrors: the black-box chiplet pad vocabulary. adk has a strict-version gate that forces its copy forward, so the spec copy goes stale by construction unless something outside both repositories says otherwise
consumers: the pads-versus-pillars alignment check reads the vocabulary to know which layers are pads
the black-box importer assumes exactly these layers when a commercial chiplet ships no .lyp
artifacts.why: the one vocabulary a closed-PDK chiplet is described in. `current` is read from the owner's file rather than declared here, so an ADK release that bumps the vocabulary does not need an edit in this repository in the same hour to stay green; the floor is what this ecosystem still reads.

consumers: the deck runner passes the method registry into the assembly DRC as a rule parameter
the export pipeline derives the per-connection interconnect method from this file

the assembly-LVS bridge reads the registry for the method each connection binds, and the attachment-sidecar derivation reaches it through this loader. Unregistered until 2026-09-17, which is why its exact-match version test survived a row that declares the rule as additive_minor
artifacts.why: the single source of truth for the post-fabrication interconnect elements. It had no row anywhere until now, so a schema_version bump had no registered consumer to notify; the consumers listed are the ones this superproject pins, which is deliberately not the whole set.

mirrors: the interconnect method registry. The PDK owns the file and the spec publishes it
artifacts.why: the schema the interconnect method registry validates against. The interconnect PDK is the authoritative author and chiplet-spec is the publisher; the row keeps the publisher as `owner` while the identity is `bytes`, where the two sides are symmetric, and the orientation is revisited in the wave that gives this row a version policy.

mirrors: the interconnect block of a .chiplet document
artifacts.why: chiplet-spec publishes the schema and the ADK validates against it. The two trees are only ever correct together, and no per-repository gate can see the other one.

declarations: the ADK suite runs the decks against this KLayout, so it has to be the one the image ships
the interposer decks are the ones most sensitive to a KLayout change, and they run on their own runner
the documentation build imports KLayout to generate figures from the same decks
the plugin declares a floor rather than a pin, and a floor raised above the image pin is an install that resolves to something else
artifacts.why: one KLayout across the ecosystem, sourced from the image ARG. Testing a deck against a different KLayout than the one that ships proves the deck works somewhere other than where it runs. `current` is the image, because the image is the only declaration there is.

mirrors: the layer registry every consumer validates against
artifacts.why: chiplet-spec publishes the schema and the ADK validates against it. The two trees are only ever correct together, and no per-repository gate can see the other one.

declarations: the export plugin's own dependencies, installed into the KiCad scripting environment
the second plugin in the same repository, with its own file and therefore its own way to drift
the converter's Qt and parsing dependencies
the ADK suite's dependencies, unpinned there because the pin set constrains them, read so a floor added later is checked against the image pin
the interposer PDK suite's dependencies, the KLayout its decks run under among them
the interconnect PDK suite's dependencies, the jsonschema its method registry is validated with among them
the KiCad plugin repository's own distribution metadata and test dependencies, beside the two per-plugin requirements files
the converter's distribution metadata, beside its requirements.txt; the two can drift apart
the documentation build, which is also where the KLayout pin is declared
the reference reader's distribution metadata, read as a dependency list rather than through a TOML parser
the conformance suite's own test dependencies. jsonschema backs the executable schema gate there, so a floor raised above the image pin is a schema gate run against a version the image does not ship
artifacts.why: every Python package the image pins, and every file in the ecosystem that declares a constraint on one of them. The declarations carry no locator because the whole file is read line by line, not at one point; the pin is what actually runs, so a floor raised above it means a repository is exercised against a version it says it does not support.
chiplet-spec publishes the schema and the ADK validates against it. The two trees are only ever correct together, and no per-repository gate can see the other one.
